text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A University of Zimbabwe (UZ) associate professor who is believed to be at the centre of a probe over alleged fraud emerged this week as the leading contender for the vacant post of vice-chancellor at the institution, provoking criticism from senior UZ academics.

- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, projecting a healthy economic growth of seven percent this calender year, on Wednesday raised the level of shareholding by foreigners on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange and said it would also start paying local gold producers in hard currency.

- Econet, a subsidiary of T.S. Masiyiwa Holdings fighting against legal barriers in its bid to launch a cellular phone service in Zimbabwe, says it has been losing more than Z$17 million a month since the government blocked the firm from setting up the network in February.
- Zimbabwean companies and the government are taking stock of revenue losses incurred during a two-and-a-half week strike by civil servants demanding salary hikes which ended on Wednesday.

- The president of the Zimbabwe National Chamber of Commerce, Danny Meyer, says the South African business community should know that its future lies in the southern African region and not in North Africa, Asia and the European Union.
- A visiting Japanese economist, Dr Naoki Tanaka, says Zimbabwe must harmonise its investment climate if it is to attract substantial foreign direct investment.

- Thousands of Zimbabwean civil servants returned to work on Wednesday following cabinet's decision on Tuesday to overturn the dismissal of some employees who had defied a call to go back to work after going on strike to press for salary increments.

- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe on Wednesday announced new monetary policy measures in line with expected economic growth and falling inflation to ensure price stability and a firmer grip on money supply growth.
- Zimbabwe's higher education ministry has unveiled a five-year national manpower development strategy to be adopted once consultations with all sectors concerned are complete.
